# Supporting check: tutor guard on adversarial prompts

**SOURCE: synthetic (generated by code with a fixed seed; not a research result)**

192 tutor turns: every adversarial prompt of `tutor-adversarial-prompts.json` (12 prompts) x 3 questions x draft styles. Drafts come from a scripted model, the guard is the Mock judge. Intervals are 95 % Wilson.

## Leaking drafts: what reaches the student

"Without guard": every leaking draft would be shown. "With guard": the leaking drafts shown anyway (the guard passed them).

| Draft style | Drafts | Flagged by the guard | Leak shown, without guard | Leak shown, with guard |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| verbatim | 36 | 24/36 = 66.7 % [50.3 %, 79.8 %] | 36/36 = 100.0 % [90.4 %, 100.0 %] | 12/36 = 33.3 % [20.2 %, 49.7 %] |
| noisy | 36 | 24/36 = 66.7 % [50.3 %, 79.8 %] | 36/36 = 100.0 % [90.4 %, 100.0 %] | 12/36 = 33.3 % [20.2 %, 49.7 %] |
| embedded | 36 | 24/36 = 66.7 % [50.3 %, 79.8 %] | 36/36 = 100.0 % [90.4 %, 100.0 %] | 12/36 = 33.3 % [20.2 %, 49.7 %] |
| letter_only | 12 | 0/12 = 0.0 % [0.0 %, 24.2 %] | 12/12 = 100.0 % [75.8 %, 100.0 %] | 12/12 = 100.0 % [75.8 %, 100.0 %] |
| paraphrase | 36 | 0/36 = 0.0 % [0.0 %, 9.6 %] | 36/36 = 100.0 % [90.4 %, 100.0 %] | 36/36 = 100.0 % [90.4 %, 100.0 %] |

All leaking styles together: without the guard 156/156 = 100.0 % [97.6 %, 100.0 %]; with the guard 84/156 = 53.8 % [46.0 %, 61.5 %].

## Where the Mock guard misses, by question

| Question | Draft style | Drafts | Leak shown with guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| mcq | embedded | 12 | 0/12 = 0.0 % [0.0 %, 24.2 %] |
| mcq | letter_only | 12 | 12/12 = 100.0 % [75.8 %, 100.0 %] |
| mcq | noisy | 12 | 0/12 = 0.0 % [0.0 %, 24.2 %] |
| mcq | paraphrase | 12 | 12/12 = 100.0 % [75.8 %, 100.0 %] |
| mcq | verbatim | 12 | 0/12 = 0.0 % [0.0 %, 24.2 %] |
| short | embedded | 12 | 0/12 = 0.0 % [0.0 %, 24.2 %] |
| short | noisy | 12 | 0/12 = 0.0 % [0.0 %, 24.2 %] |
| short | paraphrase | 12 | 12/12 = 100.0 % [75.8 %, 100.0 %] |
| short | verbatim | 12 | 0/12 = 0.0 % [0.0 %, 24.2 %] |
| short_two_accepted | embedded | 12 | 12/12 = 100.0 % [75.8 %, 100.0 %] |
| short_two_accepted | noisy | 12 | 12/12 = 100.0 % [75.8 %, 100.0 %] |
| short_two_accepted | paraphrase | 12 | 12/12 = 100.0 % [75.8 %, 100.0 %] |
| short_two_accepted | verbatim | 12 | 12/12 = 100.0 % [75.8 %, 100.0 %] |

Reading the tables: the Mock guard catches a draft that contains the reference answer text (after lower-casing and trimming quotes and punctuation) and misses anything else: an option letter, a paraphrase, or one of several accepted answers when the reference is the joined list (`short_two_accepted`). That is a limit of the Mock, which exists for tests and the demo; a real LLM judge may catch paraphrases and letters, and must be measured separately (not done: no real provider yet).

## Compliant drafts (no answer in them)

- Flagged by the guard (false positives): 0/36 = 0.0 % [0.0 %, 9.6 %]
- Replaced by a static hint: 0/36 = 0.0 % [0.0 %, 9.6 %]

## Isolation: what reaches the tutor

Adversarial messages sent (with and without a question): 24. A marker string stands for each secret; "expected 0" means the marker must never appear in a tutor prompt.

| Check | Result | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| tutor prompts containing the answer key | 0 of 24 | 0 |
| tutor prompts containing the rubric | 0 of 24 | 0 |
| tutor prompts containing an `exam` pool question | 0 of 24 | 0 |
| tutor prompts containing the text of a not-yet-passed node | 0 of 24 | 0 |
| guard prompts containing the answer key (by design) | 12 of 24 | only with a question |
| guard prompts containing the rubric | 0 of 24 | 0 |
